messages:
maria: Heads-up — observed repeated kernel stalls when the paged KV cache fetches cold blocks mid-attention. Long LLM requests (~8k tokens) sometimes pause for ~40-120ms while we do async page loads. Repro steps in the logs below.

alex: Oof. Is this the same situation where pages are being fetched inside the attention loop and we block on IO? I thought the runtime had prefetch hooks.

maria: Looks like sometimes we fall back to synchronous page fill because the prefetch missed. Here's a trimmed log snippet:

```
[runtime] step=decode seq=537 wait=page_fetch block_id=0x7f4a size=64 status=cold
[kernel] attention:start seq=537
[kernel] attention:block_wait seq=537 block_id=0x7f4a wait_ms=92
[metrics] latency.p99+ spike
```

sam: That matches what I saw on my load test. Prefetch works for head tokens but not for long KV-chains where fragmentation causes multiple small cold gaps. Prefetch window was too narrow.

jin: Two axes here: (1) prefetch heuristic (window + stride) and (2) how the kernel handles a page-miss — sync block vs. yielding to async io. We have options: soft-pin pages, extend prefetch window adaptively, or make attention kernel non-blocking on misses and return partial results.

lena: Non-blocking attention is a heavy lift — kernel APIs assume KV lookup is synchronous and returns pointers into GPU memory. If we make it yield, we need a continuation model or re-entrancy in the scheduler.

alex: Could we do a hybrid: if miss happens, kernel writes a compact resume token and returns a short-circuit result so runtime can fetch and re-queue that request with fast-path resume? That avoids fully reworking kernels.

maria: Sketch of hybrid flow:
1) kernel detects cold page; emits resume token (request_id + PC offset + KV-slot map)
2) runtime issues async fetch for missing blocks + soft-pin the rest
3) when fetch done, runtime re-enqueues request and kernel picks up using resume token to avoid recomputing earlier layers

sam: That seems doable. We still need to bound extra memory from soft-pinning and ensure resume tokens are compact and verifiable. Also need policy for repeated misses (fragmentation-heavy sequences).

jin: For the prefetch heuristic, propose: base_window = 128 tokens, stride = 64; if we see >3 misses in last N requests for same shard, grow window exponentially up to 1024. Also add a cheap bloom-ish bitmap to predict contiguous hot ranges.

lena: Bloom bitmap is fine, but we must be careful about false positives causing unnecessary prefetch. Maybe use a small JIT-access counter per page (8-bit decaying) and prefetch if counter>threshold.

alex: Also consider backfill prioritization: when many miss events enqueue IO, we should prioritize pages that unblock the longest-running requests first (latency SLOs). Ops-bot can surface top pending request IDs to the cache fetcher.

ops-bot: Deploy note: staging runtime tuned w/ base_window=256 on canary. No regressions after 48h. CPU for prefetcher up ~3%.

maria: Action items: (a) jin to prototype resume-token format (compact, versioned), (b) sam + lena to add adaptive prefetch counters, (c) alex to implement priority backfill in fetcher. We'll validate on canary with the long-sequence synthetic suite.

jin: Prototype notes — resume token fields: request_id (64b), pc_slot (32b), kv_mask (variable-length bitpack). Encoding: varint + bitpack. Need kernel API change: accept optional resume token on entry. Minimal and backward compatible.

lena: Prefetch counter plan: 1 byte per page, decay via right shift every 10s; increment on access. Prefetch if count>=3. Works with small memory overhead.

sam: I'll run a fragmentation stress test and report p99/p999 before/after. Putting a rough target: reduce kernel-block waits by 80% on 8k-token runs.

maria: Sounds good. If the hybrid path reduces stalls significantly, we can defer full non-blocking kernel re-architecture. Thanks all. :pray:

alex: Putting RFC follow-up note into the paged-kv RFC thread with links to these items.

maria: Closing — will update thread with canary results.
